instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines "lobbyist" as anyone who contracts for or receives economic consideration (other than expense reimbursement) from a principal whose duties include lobbying, with no dollar threshold.
The lobbyist definition contains no expenditure-based threshold for the lobbyist; it uses receipt of economic consideration and a 5-day communication test, not the lobbyist's own spending.

Expenditures for paid advertising and grassroots activities are only required to be included in the aggregate report if they exceed $500 during the reporting period, indicating reporting is not required for all expenditures (Tier −1).

A principal anticipating aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 in a calendar year may file a verified statement and is exempt from licensing, registration, and reporting requirements.

No statutory provision exempts a lobbyist from filing disclosure based on a percentage of their compensated time devoted to lobbying; the time test in §13.62(11) is a 5-days threshold defining lobbyist status, and exemptions in §13.621 are not time-percentage based.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell based on the Wisconsin statute text.

**row_001**: §13.62(11) defines "Lobbyist" as an individual who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses" — no dollar threshold for compensation.

**row_002**: No expenditure threshold on the lobbyist side; the $500 threshold is principal-side (§13.64(1)).

**row_003**: §13.62(11) — if duties are not exclusively lobbying, individual is a lobbyist only if they make lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period.

**row_004**: §13.68(1)(a)5 — only paid advertising/general public lobbying expenditures need be included if they exceed $500; §13.68(1)(a)6 — individual lobbyist amounts listed only if >$200.

**row_005**: §13.621(5) — principals anticipating ≤$500 in lobbying expenditures may file a verified statement and are exempt from licensing/registration/reporting.

**row_006**: No time-percentage de minimis for lobbyist filing. §13.68(1)(a) excludes from principal's reports any employee who is not a lobbyist and devotes not more than 10 hours to lobbying — that's hours, not a percentage, and is a reporting exclusion, not a lobbyist filing exemption.

input.justification: The statute defines "lobbyist" as anyone who contracts for or receives economic consideration (other than expense reimbursement) from a principal whose duties include lobbying, with no dollar threshold.
The lobbyist definition contains no expenditure-based threshold for the lobbyist; it uses receipt of economic consideration and a 5-day communication test, not the lobbyist's own spending.
If an individual's duties are not exclusively lobbying, they are a lobbyist only if they make lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period.

Expenditures for paid advertising and grassroots activities are only required to be included in the aggregate report if they exceed $500 during the reporting period, indicating reporting is not required for all expenditures (Tier −1).

A principal anticipating aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 in a calendar year may file a verified statement and is exempt from licensing, registration, and reporting requirements.

No statutory provision exempts a lobbyist from filing disclosure based on a percentage of their compensated time devoted to lobbying; the time test in §13.62(11) is a 5-days threshold defining lobbyist status, and exemptions in §13.621 are not time-percentage based.
